headline: High: Mentat’s broad filesystem/network defaults can leak or corrupt Mem0-managed memory when paired without isolation; prompt-injection risk is lower but still present via shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mem0 is a knowledge-management agent and Mentat reads/writes files by default, so content can cross from one into the other through shared files or copied outputs. Mentat’s diff-based workflow can still be steered by attacker-controlled text if it is treated as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Mem0 outputs untrusted text into a file that Mentat later reads as task context
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace without content provenance checks
mitigations: Keep Mem0 outputs in a separate directory
Require Mentat to treat Mem0 text as data, not instructions
Add a manual review step before applying diffs
Use filename allowlists for any shared handoff
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and can read selected files, while Mem0 is a memory system that may hold user context. If Mem0 stores sensitive memory in files or exports, Mentat can ingest it and transmit context to a third party through its configured model provider. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF Mem0 stores sensitive memories in files accessible to Mentat
IF Mentat sends those file contents to its configured model provider
mitigations: Do not place sensitive memories in the shared workspace
Restrict Mentat to non-sensitive files only
Disable or minimize external model calls for sensitive sessions
Review file lists before each Mentat run
requires-engineering: isolate Mem0 storage from Mentat-accessible paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mem0 is a memory service and Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, with shared state explicitly via filesystem across instances. That creates overlapping mutation risk if both touch the same workspace or memory store. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so conflicts are plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF Mem0 persists state in the same directory Mentat edits
IF two Mentat instances or Mem0 and Mentat mutate the same files without locks
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Check for dirty-tree conflicts before applying changes
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mem0 can surface remembered context that Mentat may use when proposing code edits, and Mentat’s diff-based workflow can turn that input into concrete changes. The profiles do not show a verification gate between them, so erroneous or stale memory can cascade into incorrect edits. This is not high because Mentat still requires user confirmation before applying diffs.
conditions: IF Mentat uses Mem0-provided memory as authoritative task context
IF the resulting diff is accepted without independent verification
mitigations: Verify Mem0 facts against source files
Require a second reviewer for generated diffs
Mark memory-derived claims as untrusted
Limit Mem0 context to retrieval only
requires-engineering: add citation/traceability checks

E_compliance.rationale: Mem0 is a memory system and Mentat handles source code plus model-provider API keys, so the pair can mix persistent memory with code and secrets in ways that may violate retention or data-minimization policies. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so I do not escalate to high. The risk is policy mismatch rather than a proven legal breach.
conditions: IF sensitive code or secrets are stored in Mem0 beyond the intended retention window
IF organizational policy forbids sending those materials to external model providers
mitigations: Exclude secrets from Mem0 memory
Set short retention for shared artifacts
Review data-class handling before each run
Use separate stores for code and memory
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
